content:
If you've been testing beta versions of Apple Watch apps this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has confirmed the issue and is currently pushing automatic updates on behalf of developers.

The related updates are being rolled out via the App Store, with the update notes reading: "This app has been updated by Apple in preparation for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features."

Apple notified developers earlier this week that the entire update process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, iOS 27, and other new operating systems are expected to be officially released to the public around mid-September, so these necessary updates should be completed before the official launch.

Apple explained that because some watchOS apps are experiencing issues on the arm64 architecture, this measure is necessary. Reports indicate that the company is automatically reprocessing and repackaging the affected apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning properly without any additional action required from developers.
